issues.description: Per-invocation client creation inside process_frame is wasteful and hides connection lifecycle.
issues.detail: The async with self._aws_session.client(...) opens a fresh bedrock-agentcore client on every LLMContextFrame. Boto/aioboto session+client setup is non-trivial; the right data is a long-lived client owned by the processor, started in setup and closed in cleanup. Keep the data structure (one client per processor), and the control flow becomes obvious.

issues.description: Timeout-based bookend state machine is the wrong data structure for response framing.
issues.detail: _output_response_open plus a 1s sleep task to emit LLMFullResponseEndFrame races with the final explicit close at the end of process_frame and adds three pieces of mutable state. The data is simpler than this: one invocation produces a bounded stream of parts. Emit Start once before the loop, End once after, drop the timer entirely. Data dominates; the algorithm follows.

issues.description: SSE parsing is hand-rolled and brittle; should be a small filter, not inline string surgery.
issues.detail: split('\n'), startswith('data: '), slice [6:] mixes transport parsing with business logic inside process_frame. Make it a tiny generator: bytes-in, response-line-out. Then process_frame just consumes lines and calls the response transformer. Composition over a 40-line conditional block. Also: line[6:] assumes exactly one space after 'data:', which SSE does not guarantee.

issues.description: agentArn parameter name violates PEP 8 and the rest of the file's snake_case.
issues.detail: Every other arg is snake_case (aws_access_key, aws_region) but agentArn is camelCase, presumably mirroring the AWS API field. Public Python API should be agent_arn; translate to agentRuntimeArn at the call site. Small thing, but it's the signature users will type.

issues.description: response_to_output_transformer can raise JSONDecodeError and crash the processor.
issues.detail: default_response_to_output_transformer calls json.loads with no try/except. A malformed SSE line or non-JSON single-part response will propagate out of process_frame. Either document that transformers must be total, or wrap the call site and log+skip. Prefer the latter: a transform that yields None on bad input composes cleanly.

issues.description: Default context transformer concatenates content parts with no separator discipline and ignores non-text parts silently.
issues.detail: ' '.join([part.get('text', '') for part in content]) emits empty strings for image/tool parts, producing leading/trailing/double spaces. Filter then join, or document that only text parts are supported. Tiny data-shape decision; the resulting code is one line shorter and obviously correct.

review.summary: The processor does a reasonable job wrapping AgentCore, but the framing state machine is over-engineered for what is really a bounded stream: one invocation, N parts, then done. A timer task plus an open-flag plus a final explicit close is three representations of the same fact. Strip the timer, emit Start/End around the loop, and the code shrinks and stops racing with itself. Two other small Unix-shaped wins: hoist the boto client out of the per-frame path, and pull SSE parsing into a tiny generator so process_frame reads as transform-and-push rather than transport plumbing.
